location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1: 'V's loop ends when its `rerun` holds only `adversarial`/`e2e` (contract `phase1_reuse` read off the list) and ...')
issue: The interim end rule changes the contract's meaning. The contract ends V's Phase 1 loop when V is **clean**: `phase1_reuse` true, AND none of V's per-version Layer 1/2/5 files holds a blocking finding, AND a Layer 2/5 run that reported `skipped` counts as clean (Plan > Phase 1). The spec keeps only the `rerun`-list half. Two cases break. (a) A fresh per-version Layer 1/2/5 file that holds blocking findings is `reuse: true`, so `rerun` drops that layer and the loop 'ends' with the blockers unfixed. That also contradicts 'patch and repeat as today' (today: 'ulangi ... sampai bersih'). (b) With Docker absent, ps-run-layer never writes skip payloads to disk (`if not (payload.get("versions") or {}): continue` in main). So `flashlight` and `scenario` stay in `per_version[V].rerun` forever, and the loop never ends, even though the E2E side ends through the `skipped` rule.
implementation_impact: The docs writer has to choose between the literal rule (an infinite loop when Docker is absent, and an early exit while blockers remain) and inventing a 'clean' judgment that the slice defers (`phase1_reuse`/`clean` are not emitted). Two writers would produce different SKILL.md/run-phases.md loops.
suggestion: Add an interim clean rule to the Fase 1 end condition: V's loop ends when its `rerun` holds only `adversarial`/`e2e`, and the orchestrator finds no blocking finding in V's per-version Layer 1/2/5 files (read as today), and a Layer 2/5 run that printed 'tak dijalankan'/skipped this session counts as done for that layer. Alternatively, have the plan emit `per_version[V].clean` now.

location: Design Notes > Aggregate ('`versions[ver].reason`: `e2e_state` `fail` → the first failing cell's reason (`fail`)')
issue: Two different sets go by 'failing'. `e2e_state` is `fail` when a configured cell's newest **gate-grade** record is `fail` (contract Aggregate). The Plan > Derivation predicate 'failing' that this slice imports also counts stale cold full fails, and those do not make `e2e_state` fail. Separately, a cell's plan reason comes from its newest **fresh** record. Take cold fail, then warm pass, or cold fail, then a `not-run` or crash record: the newest gate-grade record is `fail`, but the plan reason is `warm-only`, `not-run` or `inconclusive`, not `fail`. So the parenthetical '(`fail`)' can disagree with the reason the rule computes.
implementation_impact: An implementer can't tell whether `versions[ver].reason` is the literal string `fail`, the plan reason of a cell whose newest gate-grade record is `fail`, or the reason of the first cell under the Plan 'failing' predicate. Tests on `versions[ver].reason` for these histories would be written to different expectations.
suggestion: Pin it to one rule. For example: `e2e_state` `fail` → `reason` = `fail` (literal). Then, if the cell is needed, name it as the first cell in `psm_e2e_browsers` order whose newest gate-grade record is `fail`.

location: Boundaries > Always (Aggregate: `--config`, `--tag-map`/`--extra-tag-map`) vs cell-contract.md > Config keys > Image tag
issue: The contract resolves the tag in plan, runner and aggregate as `resolve_tag(parse_tag_map(--tag-map, else psm_flashlight_tag_map; --extra-tag-map), version)`. 'Config keys' is not among the contract sections the spec implements. The spec covers the plan (it keeps `apply_config_file`, which maps `psm_flashlight_tag_map` → `tag_map`) and the runner (Design Notes: its own key map reads `psm_flashlight_tag_map`). For the aggregate it names only the new `--tag-map`/`--extra-tag-map` flags. It never says the aggregate also reads `psm_flashlight_tag_map` from `--config`.
implementation_impact: A literal implementation reads only the flags. In the documented interim aggregate command (`--config <cfg>` with no `--tag-map`), a project with a custom `psm_flashlight_tag_map` then resolves the default tags in the aggregate. Every record reads `stale-tag` there while the plan reads it fresh, and `ready` can never become true.
suggestion: Add to the Aggregate bullet: the tag is resolved as `--tag-map`, else `--config` `psm_flashlight_tag_map`, then `--extra-tag-map` applied on top (same as plan and runner). Add a test with a non-default tag map supplied only through `--config`.

location: Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py ('move `SUPPORTED_ENGINES` and the default version/browser lists (drift test reads them there)')
issue: The spec doesn't name the moved constants and doesn't say which test changes. The drift checks in tests/test-ps-flashlight-run.py read `DEFAULT_BROWSERS` from ps-e2e-run.py with `_literal_const`, which raises AssertionError when the name is missing. They read each script's `--versions` default with `_argparse_default`, which resolves only an `ast.Constant` or a same-file `ast.Name`. A default written as `fl.DEFAULT_...` is an `ast.Attribute`, so it returns None and is reported as drift for ps-e2e-run.py and ps-plan-layers.py. 'Drift test reads them there' could mean the test already does this (it doesn't) or that the test must be changed (unstated).
implementation_impact: Moving the lists as told breaks the existing drift checks. The implementer must pick constant names and either rewrite the drift test or keep duplicate literals, which defeats the move.
suggestion: Name the constants (e.g. `DEFAULT_TARGET_VERSIONS`, `DEFAULT_E2E_BROWSERS` in ps-flashlight-run.py). State that test-ps-flashlight-run.py's drift checks read them from ps-flashlight-run.py, and that `_argparse_default` learns to resolve `fl.<NAME>` attributes, or that each script's argparse default stays a same-file literal or constant checked against the moved one.

location: Tasks > docs (SKILL.md 'Lapis 4' paragraph) / Design Notes > Interim orchestration
issue: Today SKILL.md's Lapis 4 visual review runs `ps-e2e-run.py ... --screenshot-dir <psm_reports_dir>/e2e-shots` directly and reviews those screenshots. In this slice direct output is never evidence. None of the interim Fase 1/2 `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e` commands carries `-- --screenshot-dir`. The contract's interim-free visual-review flow (tier-matrix Visual review, `visual-pending`) is not in scope. The spec asks for the Lapis 4 paragraph to be rewritten but never says where the screenshots for visual review come from.
implementation_impact: The docs writer must guess between three options: keep a separate direct run, which costs one extra cold boot per version just for screenshots; add `-- --screenshot-dir` to the history-mode runs; or drop visual review for now. Each choice changes cost and what the orchestrator reviews.
suggestion: Say it in the Interim orchestration: interactive runs pass `-- --screenshot-dir <psm_reports_dir>/e2e-shots` to every `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e` call, and the visual review reads the run folders from the aggregate's `e2e_screenshot_dir`. Direct `ps-e2e-run.py` runs stay for the quickstart probe only.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration ('`<cfg>` = `<psm_reports_dir>/psm-config.json`') and Boundaries > Always (Headless config copy: 'copies the resolved `<psm_reports_dir>/psm-config.json` verbatim')
issue: SKILL.md On Activation step 1 allows 'Resolver absen? Pakai default kanonik skrip'. In that case `psm-config.json` is never written. Every interim command passes `--config <cfg>`, and the headless copy is defined as a verbatim copy of that file. The spec doesn't cover the missing-file case.
implementation_impact: Following the docs literally, plan, ps-run-layer and aggregate exit 2 on an unreadable `--config`, and headless has nothing to copy. Docs writers will improvise either 'omit `--config`' (the script defaults, which in headless break the caller's narrowed set) or 'write a minimal JSON'.
suggestion: Add one sentence: when the resolver is absent, the orchestrator writes `<psm_reports_dir>/psm-config.json` holding only `psm_target_versions` and `psm_e2e_browsers` (script defaults), so `<cfg>` and the headless copy always exist.

location: Tasks > tests / I/O rows 'Crash child', 'Child exit 2', 'Stopped' / AC3
issue: Today's CLI tests replace `mod._spawn` with a fake that returns an exit code synchronously, and `execute()` submits every child to a ThreadPoolExecutor at once. The new runner starts children itself, reaps them in completion order, stops starting after a child exit 2, appends after each reap, and checks `fl.docker_available()` before spawning. The spec names no test seam for any of this. On a host without Docker, every history-mode CLI test (AC3, crash, child exit 2, probe drop) would print `skipped` and append nothing unless `docker_available` is stubbed. The 'Stopped' row (exit 143, records only for children that already exited) doesn't say how a test delivers the stop.
implementation_impact: The implementer has to design the spawn/reap seam and the stubs alone. Without a stub, the suite passes or fails depending on whether the host has Docker. The Verification command ('no FAILED line') is then not reproducible.
suggestion: State the seam: an injectable spawn function returning a handle (pid, poll/wait, output path) used by the reaping loop; tests stub `fl.docker_available` to True (and False for the skipped case); the Stopped test raises `fl.JobStopped` from the fake reaper after the first child is reaped and asserts exit 143, one version's records and no output line.

location: Design Notes > Runner interim ('`--merge-only --layer e2e` takes only `--module`, `--reports-dir`, `--config` ... the view overwrites a legacy `<module>-e2e.json`')
issue: The spec gives no exit code for the e2e report view. Today `merge_only` derives its exit code from `pass` and missing versions (1 when no per-version files exist). The view has no `pass` and is never evidence. Three cases are open: zero records anywhere, a write failure, and extra flags such as `--versions`, `--jobs` or `--session` ('takes only'). `--jobs` has an argparse default, so it can't be detected without inspecting argv.
implementation_impact: Fase 2's wrap-up runs this command right before the aggregate. If an orchestrator treats a non-zero exit as failure, it could stop the wrap-up. Tests can't assert an exit code.
suggestion: Specify: exit 0 after writing the view (including when every cell is `null`), exit 2 on input errors (an explicit `--versions`/`--cells`/`--session`/passthrough, a bad config) or a write failure; `--jobs`/`--verbose` are ignored.

location: Boundaries > Always ('prints the Runner > Output JSON line') / cell-contract.md > Runner > Output
issue: The output line has a `reason` key, but neither the spec nor the contract says what it holds. Is it null on `ran`? On `skipped`, is it the ps-run-layer docker message or the child's `reason` string, and which child's when several reported skipped? And for a post-spawn exit 2, what does the line carry?
implementation_impact: The docs and the orchestrator read this line. Tests asserting the exact line would be written to different values.
suggestion: Pin it: `reason` = null for `ran`; for `skipped`, 'docker unavailable' from ps-run-layer's own check, else the first skipped child's `reason` in completion order; for exit 2, `e2e_status` `ran` with `reason` naming the version whose child exited 2.

location: Boundaries > Always (Aggregate list) vs cell-contract.md > Aggregate (record-selection bullet: `e2e_browsers_run`, `layers_run.e2e`, `e2e_screenshot_dir`, `e2e_smoke_only`)
issue: The spec lists the aggregate pieces it builds but leaves out the other E2E fields the contract derives from selected records. They have to be rebuilt anyway, because the `--e2e` file is gone. `e2e_screenshot_dir` = 'the distinct run folders of the selected records' `screenshots`' is underspecified. Records carry no `screenshot_dir` (the Fields whitelist drops it), so the run folder must be inferred from each screenshot path (`<base>/run-<ts>/<ver>/<file>`). Today `e2e_smoke_only`, `e2e_browsers` and `e2e_browsers_run` are emitted only when `e2e_ran`, and the spec doesn't say whether that condition becomes 'some configured cell has a record'.
implementation_impact: These fields feed SKILL.md 'Vonis dan output' and the headless return (`e2e_smoke_only`, `layers_run`). Without a rule, the implementer guesses how to derive the path and when each field is emitted.
suggestion: State explicitly that the remaining contract Aggregate fields are in scope. Define `e2e_screenshot_dir` as the distinct `parents[1]` (run folder) of the selected records' screenshot paths, an empty list or absent when none. Say `e2e_smoke_only`/`e2e_browsers`/`e2e_browsers_run` are emitted when `layers_run.e2e` is true.

location: Boundaries > Always (`ps-e2e-run.py`: 'exit 3 on any failing cell')
issue: The spec adds exit 3 but doesn't restate the 0/1 split. Today, a version where one engine launch-fails (or is dropped by the probe) and the other passes gives `r["pass"] = True`, so the exit is 0. The contract says 0 only when 'every driven cell passes', and 1 'otherwise (infra failure or inconclusive cell)'. A launch-error cell is inconclusive, and it did enter its `browser:<engine>` phase.
implementation_impact: Direct runs (the quickstart probe, Lapis 4) and test-ps-e2e-run.py's exit-code assertions depend on this. Implementers will differ on whether the case keeps exit 0 or becomes exit 1.
suggestion: Add: exit 0 only when every cell the child emits is `pass`; any emitted inconclusive cell (launch error, boot or install failure) → 1; probe-dropped engines alone do not change the exit code (or do, but say which).

issue: Per-cell field types are not pinned. `console_errors` is an int count at version level today, while the per-scenario data is a list, and the contract Fields don't say which. It is unclear whether `scenarios_run` ('spec `name` list') includes `psm-universal-smoke`, which is builtin, not a spec. For a launch-error cell, `scenarios_run`, `authored_assertions` and `findings` could be `[]`/0 or `null` ('null for fields no engine produced').
implementation_impact: Records from different implementations stay valid but differ. The incomplete-record rule makes `authored_assertions: null` matter only on pass/fail, but tests on the child shape and the aggregate's `e2e_cells` would assert different values.
suggestion: Pin these: `console_errors` = int count for that engine; `scenarios_run` = names actually driven including `psm-universal-smoke` first; a launch-error cell has `scenarios_run: []`, `findings: []`, `inconclusive: []`, `authored_assertions: 0`.

location: Design Notes > Normalizer input ('a comma-separated string ... or a list of strings') vs ps-plan-layers.py `--versions` filled by `apply_config_file`
issue: The normalizer accepts a YAML list for `psm_target_versions`, and resolve-psm-config.py passes a list through unchanged when config.yaml holds one. The plan still fills `--versions` through `fl.apply_config_file`, which copies the raw list into `args.versions`. `main` then calls `args.versions.split(",")`, which raises AttributeError and exits with a traceback, not exit 2. The spec doesn't say whether the plan's `--versions` (run scope) also goes through the normalizer, though it does say 'a plan `--versions` entry that is not exactly a configured string is exit 2'.
implementation_impact: List support works for the configured set but crashes the plan's run-scope path for the same config. The implementer must decide whether to normalize `--versions` too.
suggestion: State that the plan's `--versions` (explicit or filled from config) is parsed with the same normalizer before the configured-string check, or that `apply_config_file` joins list values with ','.

location: Design Notes > Child output in history mode ('The probe-drop note is keyed to the dropped engine, so it lands in no emitted cell') and Record ('Version-level child fields ... go into every record of that version, `browser-unavailable` included')
issue: The note keyed to the dropped engine is the only explanation of why that engine never ran. ps-run-layer writes the dropped engine's `browser-unavailable` record, but `browser_notes` is per-cell and isn't in the list of version-level fields copied in. The spec doesn't say whether that record carries the keyed note or `browser_notes: null`.
implementation_impact: The operator-facing explanation (e.g. 'run playwright install firefox') either appears in `e2e_cells` or silently disappears, depending on the implementer.
suggestion: Say that ps-run-layer copies the child's note for the dropped engine (from a version-level `browser_notes` map keyed by engine) into that engine's `browser-unavailable` record, else `[]`.

location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2: 'an appended `fail` re-enters Fase 1 for that version (interactive)') vs 'V's E2E loop ended ... while the plan's `source_fingerprint` equals the one printed by V's last E2E run'
issue: Right after the Fase 2 run appends a `fail`, the fingerprint is unchanged, so V's E2E loop counts as ended. If Fase 1 for V checks its end condition before the operator patches, it ends at once and Fase 2 resumes with the failure still in place. The spec doesn't fix the order inside a re-entered Fase 1 iteration (patch first, or plan first).
implementation_impact: The docs can describe a re-entry that is a no-op, or a loop that requires a patch before re-planning. Two readings lead to different operator flows.
suggestion: Add: on re-entry after a Fase 2 `fail`, the first Fase 1 iteration for V starts with the operator's patch (or the 'stop' choice), then re-plans.

location: I/O matrix row 'Bad config' / Design Notes > Runner interim ('Configured-set validation ... apply to layer `e2e` only')
issue: The row lists `webkitx`, `9.1`+`9.1.0`, an empty list and a non-dotted version → exit 2, but doesn't say which entry points must reject them: plan, `ps-run-layer --layer e2e`, `--merge-only --layer e2e`, aggregate, and direct `ps-e2e-run.py --browsers`. Meanwhile `ps-run-layer` for flashlight/scenario must forward the same bad config without validating it.
implementation_impact: The test task can satisfy the row by testing the normalizer function once, or by testing every CLI. Coverage of the runner's 'e2e only' scoping stays untested either way.
suggestion: List the CLIs the row covers (plan, run-layer e2e, merge-only e2e, aggregate, ps-e2e-run `--browsers`), and add one assertion that `--layer flashlight` with the same config does not exit 2.
